alfredSkill.name: Incident Postmortem
alfredSkill.agentFacingDescription: Guidelines to write an incident postmortem: timeline, impact, root cause and follow-up actions.
alfredSkill.userFacingDescription: Write incident postmortems following the internal template.
alfredSkill.instructions:
# Incident Postmortem

When writing a postmortem, always produce the following sections:

## Summary
One paragraph describing what broke, for whom, and for how long.

## Timeline
A bulleted, timestamped list of events, from the first symptom to the resolution.

## Impact
Quantify the impact: number of affected users, failed requests, revenue at risk.

## Root cause
Explain the technical root cause, and the reason it was not caught earlier.

## Follow-up actions
List concrete, owned action items. Never write "be more careful".

currentUserSkill.name: Release Notes Writer
currentUserSkill.agentFacingDescription: Guidelines to turn a list of merged pull requests into user-facing release notes.
currentUserSkill.userFacingDescription: Turn merged pull requests into readable release notes.
currentUserSkill.instructions:
# Release Notes

Group changes under three headings: **New**, **Improved**, **Fixed**.

- One line per change, written from the user's point of view.
- No internal ticket numbers, no commit hashes.
- Skip purely internal refactors.
currentUserSkill.instructionsHtml:
Release Notes

Group changes under three headings: New, Improved, Fixed.

  • One line per change, written from the user's point of view.
  • No internal ticket numbers, no commit hashes.
  • Skip purely internal refactors.

alfredPrivateSpaceSkill.name: Space Restricted Procedures
alfredPrivateSpaceSkill.agentFacingDescription: Guidelines to answer questions about the procedures documented in the restricted space.
alfredPrivateSpaceSkill.userFacingDescription: Answer questions about the procedures of the restricted space.
alfredPrivateSpaceSkill.instructions:
# Space Restricted Procedures

Answer only from the documents of the restricted space. Cite the document for every statement, and say so when the procedures do not cover the question.
